caps.text: CALTECH, CALIFORNIA
Swiss astronomer Fritz Zwicky was stuck on a strange calculation
About 300 million light-years away...
...a giant swarm of more than 1,000 galaxies
THE COMA CLUSTER
He calculated how fast its galaxies were moving
...and something didn't add up
The galaxies were racing far too fast
Even the gravity of all the visible stars couldn't hold them
The cluster should have flown apart long ago
Yet it held together...
...as if an invisible hand was holding it
Zwicky gave the unknown stuff a name...
"DUNKLE MATERIE"
DARK MATTER
Almost 100 years later, the mystery is still unsolved
1.5 km underground, a detector recorded a collision...
...that no one has been able to explain
To hold the Coma Cluster together, Zwicky's numbers needed...
100 TIMES THE VISIBLE MASS
The number was so strange...
...most astronomers dismissed it as a measurement error
Zwicky was also famous for his fiery temper
...and he was often not taken seriously
Slowly, the idea was buried in the pages of an old research paper
The Coma Cluster kept quietly turning...
...and with it, a question nobody could answer
For the next 40 years...
...the world almost forgot this hidden mass
THE 1970s
The forgotten question came back to life...
...this time through American astronomer Vera Rubin
Rubin and her colleague Kent Ford were measuring how fast galaxies spin
...starting with the neighbouring galaxy, ANDROMEDA
In the Solar System, the rule is simple
The farther a planet is from the Sun, the slower it moves
EARTH: ~30 km/s
NEPTUNE: only ~5 km/s
Galaxies should work the same way...
...fast stars near the center, slow ones at the edge
But Rubin's data told a different story
Stars at the very edge moved just as fast as those near the center
At that speed, they should have been flung out of the galaxy
Yet the galaxy stayed intact
Galaxy after galaxy, the same result
It could only mean one thing
Something heavy and invisible fills and surrounds every galaxy
ZWICKY WAS RIGHT
Vera Rubin died in 2016...
...without ever receiving a Nobel Prize
Today, one of the world's most advanced observatories, in Chile, bears her name
VERA C. RUBIN OBSERVATORY
After Rubin's discovery, the picture of galaxies changed forever
THE MILKY WAY: about 100,000 light-years across
100+ BILLION STARS
But this glowing disk is only the inner part of the galaxy
Around it spreads a vast, invisible sphere...
THE DARK MATTER HALO
More than 10 times wider than the visible galaxy
About 90% of the Milky Way's mass is in this halo
This galaxy of billions of stars...
...is really a small disc of light, floating in an invisible ocean
And it's not just the Milky Way
Almost every big galaxy was born inside a halo like this...
...and grew up inside it
So vast, yet completely invisible
HUBBLE · JAMES WEBB · RADIO DISHES · X-RAY TELESCOPES
These machines can see the universe in every wavelength of light
...from radio waves to gamma rays
But none of them can see dark matter
It has no connection with light at all
It doesn't shine. It doesn't absorb light. It doesn't reflect it.
There's only one sign that it exists...
GRAVITY
Just like the wind: never seen itself...
...but swaying branches tell its story
Dark matter's story is written by moving galaxies and racing stars
But gravity leaves one more mark
1915: ALBERT EINSTEIN
Heavy objects bend space and time...
...and light travelling along that curve bends too
GRAVITATIONAL LENSING
When light from a distant galaxy passes dark matter, it bends
The galaxy looks stretched, warped, or even like a glowing ring
By reading these distortions backwards...
...astronomers learned to map where dark matter is, and how much
Hubble images of a galaxy cluster 5 billion light-years away...
...revealed a giant RING of dark matter
For the first time, something invisible had been mapped
Still, some scientists had doubts
What if dark matter doesn't exist at all...
...and gravity itself works differently on huge scales?
The biggest answer came from a cosmic collision
Billions of light-years away, two giant galaxy clusters collided
After the crash, the smaller cluster is racing away at...
~4,700 KM PER SECOND
The pair was named...
THE BULLET CLUSTER
Most normal matter in a cluster is extremely hot gas...
...so hot that it glows in X-rays
In the crash, the gas slowed down and got stuck in the middle
But when lensing mapped the real mass...
...most of it wasn't with the gas at all
It had passed straight through, without stopping
When the image was released in 2006...
...it became the most direct proof that dark matter exists
Now the question was: how much of it is there?
The answer was hidden in the Big Bang's leftover light...
THE COSMIC MICROWAVE BACKGROUND
...ESA's Planck satellite measured it in extreme detail
The result was stunning
85% OF ALL MATTER IS DARK MATTER
For every 1 kg of normal matter, about 5 kg of dark matter
Stars, planets, gas, dust and every living thing...
...all together, just 15%
Counting all the energy in the universe...
...normal matter is only 5%
Dark matter: about 27%
The other 68%: DARK ENERGY
A completely different mystery, speeding up the universe's expansion
Dark matter pulls things together. Dark energy pushes them apart.
The universe humans watched and measured for centuries...
...is only 5% of the whole picture
But dark matter doesn't just hold galaxies together
IT BUILT THEM
For about 380,000 years after the Big Bang...
...normal matter was so tangled with light, it couldn't clump anywhere
Light had no effect on dark matter
So gravity started pulling it together first...
...weaving a giant web of threads and knots across the universe
THE COSMIC WEB
When normal matter broke free, it fell into these dark matter wells
There, gas gathered. The first stars lit up. The first galaxies formed.
JWST has found galaxies shining just 300 million years after the Big Bang
Without dark matter, galaxies would have taken far longer to form
Maybe there would be no Milky Way, no Sun, no Earth...
...and no life
And this invisible web isn't far away
IT'S RIGHT HERE
The Sun orbits the Milky Way's center at about 230 km/s...
...carrying the whole Solar System with it
But the dark matter halo doesn't rotate like that
So as it moves, Earth is constantly passing through...
A DARK MATTER WIND
Right now it flows through walls, mountains, oceans and every human body...
...without hitting anything, without leaving a trace
Near Earth, dark matter is spread so thin...
...an Earth-sized ball of it would weigh less than 1 kg
But across the whole galaxy, it adds up to...
~1 TRILLION SUNS
After almost 100 years of searching, the biggest question remains...
WHAT IS DARK MATTER?
The hunt to catch it never stops
SOUTH DAKOTA, USA
1.5 km underground sits a detector called LZ
...filled with about 10 tonnes of liquid xenon
At that depth, radiation from above can't reach it
If a single dark matter particle hits a xenon atom...
...a faint flash of light could catch it
1 SEPTEMBER 2026
The LZ team announced a strange result
220 days of data. Just ONE collision...
...that nothing known can explain
The chance it's a fluke: about 1 in 200
A confirmed discovery needs about 1 in 3.5 million
The team was clear: it is NOT claiming to have seen dark matter
If it isn't dark matter, the list of candidates is still long
WIMPs: heavy particles
AXIONS: maybe billions of times lighter than an electron
Tiny black holes born in the Big Bang
Or maybe dark matter doesn't exist at all...
...and the laws of gravity are incomplete at the scale of galaxies
85% of the universe's matter is everywhere...
...holding every galaxy together...
...passing through every human being...
NOBODY KNOWS WHAT IT IS
Perhaps the universe's greatest discovery is still to come
And the day the secret of dark matter is revealed...
...humanity may finally understand its true place in this vast universe
